verses.text: When Jesus finished teaching, he left Galilee and went to the Judea region beyond the Jordan.
Huge crowds followed him, and he healed them there.
The Pharisees came to test him: “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason at all?”
He answered, “Haven’t you read that from the beginning the Creator made them male and female?”
“And he said, ‘That’s why a man leaves his father and mother, joins his wife, and the two become one flesh.’”
“So they’re no longer two, but one. What God joined together, no person should split apart.”
They asked him, “Then why did Moses tell us to give a divorce certificate and send her away?”
He told them, “Moses allowed you to divorce your wives because your hearts were hard. But that wasn’t how it was from the beginning.”
“I’m telling you, whoever divorces his wife—except because of sexual immorality—and marries another woman commits adultery. Whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery too.”
His disciples said, “If that’s how it is between a husband and wife, maybe it’s better not to marry.”
He answered, “Not everyone can accept this teaching—only those it’s been given to.”
“Some are eunuchs from birth; some were made eunuchs by other people; and some made themselves eunuchs for Heaven’s Kingdom. Let whoever can accept this accept it.”
Then people brought little children to Jesus so he could lay his hands on them and pray. The disciples told them off.
But Jesus said, “Let the children come to me. Don’t block them—the Kingdom of Heaven belongs to people like them.”
He laid his hands on them and then left that place.
Someone came up and asked him, “Good teacher, what good thing should I do to have eternal life?”
He said, “Why call me good? No one is good except God alone. But if you want to enter life, keep the commandments.”
The man asked, “Which ones?” Jesus answered, “‘Don’t murder. Don’t commit adultery. Don’t steal. Don’t give false testimony.”
“‘Honor your father and mother,’ and, ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’”
The young man said, “I’ve kept all those since I was young. What am I still missing?”
Jesus told him, “If you want to be complete, go sell what you own, give the money to the poor, and you’ll have treasure in heaven. Then come follow me.”
When the young man heard that, he went away sad. He had a lot of possessions.
Jesus told his disciples, “I’m telling you the truth: it’s hard for a rich person to enter Heaven’s Kingdom.”
“Let me put it another way: a camel can get through a needle’s eye more easily than a rich person can enter God’s Kingdom.”
The disciples were stunned when they heard this. “Then who can be saved?” they asked.
Jesus looked at them and said, “People can’t make it happen, but with God anything is possible.”
Peter answered, “Look, we left everything to follow you. What do we get?”

Jesus said, “I’m telling you the truth: when everything is renewed and the Son of Man sits on his glorious throne, you who followed me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging Israel’s twelve tribes.”
“Everyone who left houses, brothers, sisters, father, mother, wife, children, or land for my name will receive a hundred times as much and inherit eternal life.”
“But many who are first will be last, and many who are last will be first.”
